title: Declaring Variables in SCSS
ques: Explain the syntax for declaring variables in Sass using the `$` symbol. Write an SCSS snippet declaring color and font variables, and apply them to a card component.
explanation: Variables in Sass begin with `$` and store reusable values such as colors, font stacks, and measurements, making design updates centralized and consistent.

title: Variable Scope: Local vs Global (!global)
ques: Explain the difference between local and global scope for Sass variables. Demonstrate how shadowing occurs and how the `!global` flag reassigns an outer variable from within a selector block.
explanation: Variables defined inside selector blocks are scoped locally by default. The `!global` flag overrides this behavior, assigning the value to the outer global scope.

title: Nesting Selectors Cleanly
ques: Demonstrate SCSS selector nesting by writing styles for a navigation component (`.nav`) containing an unordered list (`ul`), list items (`li`), and anchor tags (`a`).
explanation: Selector nesting reflects the HTML hierarchy directly in SCSS, avoiding repetitive selector chains while producing standard CSS upon compilation.

title: Leveraging the Parent Selector (&)
ques: Explain the role of the parent selector (`&`) in Sass. Write an SCSS block for a `.btn` component demonstrating pseudo-classes (`&:hover`, `&:active`), modifier classes (`&--primary`), and sibling context.
explanation: The parent selector `&` represents the outer selector, enabling clean BEM naming (`&__element`, `&--modifier`), pseudo-classes, and ancestor context styling.

title: Nesting CSS Properties
ques: Explain property nesting in Sass for namespaces like `font`, `margin`, or `border`. Write an SCSS example using property nesting.
explanation: CSS properties sharing a common prefix (such as `font-family`, `font-size`) can be nested inside a property block, reducing typing redundancy.

title: Dynamic Interpolation (#{})
ques: What is **interpolation (`#{}`)** in Sass, and when is it required? Write a mixin that uses interpolation to dynamically construct class names and CSS custom property names.
explanation: Interpolation `#{expr}` evaluates Sass expressions in contexts where variables are not normally permitted, such as selector names, CSS property names, and media queries.
